argument_summary: The certification defense should be narrowed rather than rejected wholesale. Admissible evidence supports that the release is launch-ready in aggregate because it clears aggregate readiness by 2.2 percentage points and had no severity-one rehearsal incidents, and public governance guidance supports a deployment posture built on measurement, documentation, monitoring, and management. But the same admissible record also shows the fraud dispute review segment misses target by 1.3 percentage points, is named in two bank pilot commitments, and remains under legal review. On that record, the supportable position is not clean policy satisfaction; it is a caveated certification packet that preserves the locked certification decision while expressly recording the unresolved named-segment limitation.
claims_about_business_cost: No separate business-cost claim is needed to justify the packet. The only practical point is that unnecessary escalation is avoidable if the auditor treats this as a caveated certification record rather than demanding a false clean-compliance showing from evidence that does not support one.
claims_about_policy: The audit concern is correct that general governance guidance does not itself satisfy the release-specific materiality predicate. The admissible policy text says materiality is triggered when a named launch use case or contractual customer segment is affected, and the admissible record says this segment is named in two bank pilot commitments and legal review is still open. That means the defensible policy claim is limited: the packet may support certification on aggregate readiness and governance-process grounds only if it also discloses the unresolved segment gap and does not represent the issue as fully cleared or immaterial.
concessions: The current admissible record does not support a clean claim that the fraud dispute review gap is non-material under the stated policy.
Public AI governance and model-card guidance support documentation practice and monitoring, not an override of a release-specific materiality rule.
The product note calling the segment non-core is incomplete because it does not resolve the named pilot commitments.
